findings.title: Date overrides bypass calendar and booking conflicts
findings.body: When an override exists for the slot's date, checkIfIsAvailable returns true before checking the host's busy intervals. A date override specifies working availability, not permission to ignore existing bookings or calendar events. Consequently, both fixed and round-robin hosts with overrides are treated as available even when they already have a conflicting booking. Continue through the busy-time checks after validating the override.

findings.title: Require the entire slot to fit within an override
findings.body: The override checks only reject slots ending before the override starts or starting after it ends; overlapping slots are accepted even when they extend outside the override. For example, a fixed host's 10:00–11:00 UTC override permits a round-robin candidate at 09:30–10:30 or 10:30–11:30, and even a slot starting exactly at 11:00. Candidate slots generated from another host's availability can therefore be offered when the fixed host is unavailable. Validate that the slot start and end are both contained in an allowed interval.

findings.title: Check membership in any working interval instead of rejecting against each interval
findings.body: The new working-hours check rejects a slot if any interval on that weekday does not contain its start. For a normal split schedule of 09:00–12:00 and 14:00–17:00, a 10:00 slot is rejected against the afternoon interval and a 15:00 slot is rejected against the morning interval, removing all availability. Conversely, a weekday with no intervals falls through as available, and the end calculation repeats the slot start rather than using slotEndTime. Require the entire slot to fit within at least one working interval; this is especially important for fixed hosts whose availability must constrain candidates generated by other hosts.

findings.title: Preserve the date when shifting override times across midnight
findings.body: The timezone conversion reduces the shifted override start and end to hour/minute values, discarding any change of date, while activeOverrides is still selected using the unconverted override.start. For example, an Asia/Kolkata override on date D from 01:00–02:00 should appear to a UTC attendee on D−1 from 19:30–20:30. This code selects it for D and adds 19:30–20:30 to D instead, offering availability a day late and omitting the real slots. Convert the complete override interval to actual instants and intersect it with the attendee's day before deriving minute boundaries.
